key_insight: Adaptive reinforcement learning attackers can learn to evade BB84 detection far more effectively than fixed-rate analytical eavesdropping strategies.
engineering_relevance: Quantum key distribution evaluations should include adaptive adversary models, since security margins can change dramatically under learning-based attacks.
method: Modeled Eve as an MDP that observes QBER feedback and chooses intercept-or-pass actions qubit by qubit.
Compared tabular Q-Learning, SARSA, and Double Q-Learning under three channel noise levels.
Validated results across five random seeds, 45 runs per condition, and 10,000 episodes per run.
evidence_signal: At μch=1%, Q-Learning reduced detection from 99.4% to 0.28%±0.27% while extracting about 10.5 correct bits per episode, with a statistically significant difference (p=0.020).
watch_item: Results come from a tabular RL setting and a simplified attack policy, so real hardware constraints, richer quantum attacks, and protocol-specific defenses may alter the outcome.
paper_title: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Eavesdropping in BB84 Quantum Key Distribution
